answer: Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a umber index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Because the wharf index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the walnut audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 154 aliases thus needs 154 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
